posts.hook: The knee pain you keep icing may start two joints lower.
posts.body:
The knee pain you keep icing may start two joints lower.

Stand barefoot, feet under your hips, and look straight down at your inner arches.

If they sink toward the floor and your ankles roll in, your base is collapsing. A base that rolls in doesn't stay a foot problem. The shin turns to follow it, and the low back settles the tab at the top.

For years I watched people treat the joint that hurt while the real culprit sat inside their shoe.

Build control from the ground up. That's where the chain starts.

posts.hook: If your shoulder catches reaching for a seatbelt, don't blame the shoulder.
posts.body:
If your shoulder catches reaching for a seatbelt, don't blame the shoulder.

Stand with your back to a wall and press your low back flat against it. Raise both arms overhead and try to touch the backs of your hands to the wall, keeping that low back flat.

If your hands stop short, or your back peels off the wall to let them through, there's your answer. Your shoulders can't get cleanly overhead, so your spine arches to finish the reach. Every overhead move borrows from your lower back, and your back pays the interest.

This is the tech-neck body: a rounded upper back and shoulders that lost their last inches of overhead range without you noticing.

Give the range back to the joint that lost it, and your back stops covering for it.

posts.hook: Give me 60 seconds, a wall, and a chair, and I'll show you where your body breaks down first.
posts.body:
Give me 60 seconds, a wall, and a chair, and I'll show you where your body breaks down first.

Most people wait for pain to tell them something's wrong. By then the compensation is years old. The body leaks long before it hurts, and the leaks are visible if you know the seven spots to check.

Can you touch the back of your head to a wall without craning up? Do your knees hold their line when you squat? Can you stand out of a chair without your hands? Each check takes seconds, and each failed one points to a link in the chain that's gone quiet.

Don't spend another year managing pain you could measure. Count your tells. Under three, you're moving well. Three or more, you're carrying movement debt, and it compounds every year you leave it.

I put all seven into one free self-test. No equipment, no floor work. A wall, a chair, a mirror.
